newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to open diplomatic office in Russia Far East.
newsitem.headline: Japan to open diplomatic office in Russia Far East.

text.p: Japan will open a branch consulate office on an island in the Russian Far East in what could be a key policy shift to resolve a long-running territorial dispute with Moscow, Kyodo news agency said on Sunday.
Quoting unnamed foreign ministry sources, Kyodo said Tokyo would open a branch office in Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk on southern Sakhalin Island next spring.
Japan hoped to normalise its relations with the Sakhalin provincial government by setting up the office, a foreign ministry official was quoted as saying.
The move could be taken to mean that Japan would reverse its policy and effectively recognise Russia's control over the southern half of Sakhalin Island, Kyodo said.
Japanese officials were not immediately available for comment on the report.

In the 1951 San Francisco Peace Treaty signed between Japan and the Allied powers, Japan renounced all rights to the Kurile Islands and the southern half of Sakhalin Island. The Soviet Union did not sign the treaty.
Japan did not acknowledge Soviet sovereignty over the islands.

The row over the islands, called the Southern Kuriles by Russia and the Northern Territories by Japan, has stopped the two countries from signing a formal World War Two peace treaty and frozen bilateral ties for most of the last 50 years.
The move reported by Kyodo was part of Japan's long-term strategy to rosolve the territorial dispute, a senior Foreign Ministry official was quoted as saying.
Russia says the islands were part of territory promised to them at the Yalta Conference of World War Two allies.
But Japan has insisted the four islands belonged to it as far back as 1856 when the Tokugawa Shogunate signed its first treaty with Czarist Russia.

During his visit to Japan last month, Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov proposed that Tokyo and Moscow jointly develop the islands. Japan remained non-committal saying it would consider details, if any, of the proposal.
